extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering based on ConceptNet. Crowd-workers author multiple-choice questions that mention a source concept and discriminate between target concepts sharing the same semantic relation. The dataset contains 12,247 questions.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor; Jonathan Herzig; Nicholas Lourie; Jonathan Berant
extraction.citeAs: Talmor, Alon; Herzig, Jonathan; Lourie, Nicholas; Berant, Jonathan. COMMONSENSE QA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was generated in three steps: (1) subgraphs were extracted from ConceptNet, each with one source concept and three target concepts sharing the same relation; (2) Amazon Mechanical Turk workers authored three questions per subgraph, added two additional distractors per question, and a disjoint group of workers verified question quality; (3) textual context was added by querying Google search and retrieving web snippets for each question-answer candidate pair.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source was ConceptNet, a graph knowledge base containing 32 million triplets. Additional textual context was collected from Google search result snippets for each question and candidate answer.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Triplets from ConceptNet were filtered by removing general relations or relations already well explored in NLP, filtering concepts longer than four words or not in English, and filtering triplets where the edit distance between the two concepts was too low. The remaining triplets were grouped into question sets of one question concept and three answer concepts sharing the same relation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors filtered ConceptNet triplets using relation, language, concept length, and edit-distance rules, resulting in 236,208 triplets. These were grouped into approximately 130,000 triplets forming 43,000 question sets. Questions were then filtered through verification, and only questions verified by at least one worker who answered correctly were kept, filtering out 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were shown a question concept and three answer concepts and asked to formulate three questions, each containing the question concept and having one of the answer concepts as the correct answer but not the other two. Workers were instructed to avoid simple surface clues. They also added two distractors per question: one selected from ConceptNet answer concepts with the same relation to the question concept and one written manually. A disjoint group of workers verified the generated questions by either marking them unanswerable or selecting the right answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question was verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly were used. This verification process filtered out 15% of the questions. Annotators were only accepted for question generation if at least 75% of the questions they formulated passed verification.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the dataset is intended to facilitate future work in incorporating commonsense knowledge into natural language understanding systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that because questions are generated freely by workers, they often require background knowledge that is trivial to humans but is seldom explicitly reported on the web due to reporting bias. It also discusses concerns from prior work about annotation artifacts and distributional biases in commonsense datasets, motivating careful benchmark construction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper reports that 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions, which may limit diversity. It also notes that web snippets do not appear to carry much useful information for the task. The dataset is designed to be easier for humans than current models, and model performance remains substantially below human accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for commonsense question answering and evaluation of natural language understanding models. The authors split the data into training, development, and test sets with an 80/10/10 split and use it to train, validate, and test QA models.
